newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower in active trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended lower against its American counterpart on Monday, partly reflecting the U.S. dollar's firmness in overseas markets, dealers said.
The local dollar finished at T$27.445 to the U.S. dollar against Saturday's T$27.442 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$224 million.
"Buying and selling interests are fairly balanced today," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said persistent demand for the local unit before the February 7 Chinese lunar new year was largely offsetting the U.S. dollar's strength against most major currencies.
A U.S. dollar rise typically has the effect of pressuring the Taiwan dollar lower.
A range of T$27.43-47 was seen for Tuesday.
